name: Bayern Munich 2012/13 (Heynckes treble)
scopeNote: Bayern Munich under Jupp Heynckes, 2012/13: DFL-Supercup 12 Aug 2012 (first competitive match, per Wikipedia) to the DFB-Pokal final v Stuttgart on 1 June 2013 (last match; Wikipedia says 'due to play ... on 1 June'; the Champions League final v Dortmund was 25 May 2013). Pre-season friendlies excluded. Style terms used by sources: 4-2-3-1 that morphs into a 4-4-2 / '4-4-2-0' block; Spielverlagerung 'position-orientated zonal marking' with situational man orientation in counter-pressing ('access orientation'); Ballverliebt 'relativ strikt Mann gegen Mann' in the Barcelona midfield; Breaking The Lines says the centre-backs man-marked. The popular label 'gegenpressing like Dortmund' is not supported: Spielverlagerung measured fewer interceptions and more provoked challenges. Several match dates use season YYYY/YY where the source gave no day (HSV 9-2 analysis: Spielverlagerung page date 2013-07-02 is a repost date; Bayern-Hamburg was a 2012/13 league match). Source article dates come from digest metadata and some are repost dates (Wikipedia, Bleacher Report 1631044). The earlier-found fact that Bayern had a 2011/12 runner-up season is outside this profile.
openQuestions: Marking: Spielverlagerung (2013) says 'position-orientated zonal marking' in a 4-4-2-0 block; Ballverliebt (2013-04-24) says strict man-to-man in midfield v Barcelona (Schweinsteiger on Xavi, Martinez on Iniesta, Muller on Busquets); Breaking The Lines (2022) says centre-backs man-marked. Treat as zonal block with situational man orientation in midfield and in counter-pressing; confirm label.

Pressing height: Ballverliebt says the pressing line was around the halfway line or slightly in Barca's half; Breaking The Lines says Heynckes wanted to win the ball 'as high as possible'; Bleacher Report says containment; Spielverlagerung says Bayern sat in a compact 4-4-2-0 and shifted. The Dortmund final analyses say Bayern's centre-backs dropped deeper in the first 30 minutes.

Squad age and rotation: no source found with squad age or appearance counts; only partial evidence (Pizarro 33, rotation of three strikers, Kroos/Shaqiri/Muller rotation, youth debuts in April 2013 after the title was won). Sport1 piece about Boateng and Muller on the bench appeared only in a search summary.

Heynckes's own 2013 tactical words: UEFA 'Bayern's Barcelona master plan' (Heynckes and Ribery) was not accessible; stated view is limited to short post-match quotes (Football Espana, Sports Mole, Telegraph via Bleacher Report) and a kicker column quoted by Heidelberg24 (undated).
Set pieces: only StatsBomb (final) and Spielverlagerung (Barcelona tie) cover them; no season-wide data.
Coaches' Voice, Zonal Marking (Michael Cox) and Jonathan Wilson pieces on this exact season were not found; the Coaches' Voice hit was a 2021 Bayern-Barcelona piece (not this team).

sources.title: Counterpressing variations (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: In most cases, the opposing ball carrier is not pressed by the entire team but by one or two nearby players, while the others are not fixed to their positions, but take on the nearest opponent in a kind of man coverage. This brief situational man orientation ensures that after the enemy passes the players can always obtain access and challenge for the ball.

sources.title: Counterpressing variations (Spielverlagerung)

influences: Louis van Gaal (zonal shielding / counter-press concept, per Breaking The Lines)
Arrigo Sacchi (4-4-2 block with attackers as first defenders, per These Football Times)

confidence.reason: Several tier A-B sources agree on shape, build-up with Neuer and a bank of three, compactness and the Barcelona/Dortmund games (Spielverlagerung 2013, Ballverliebt 2013, StatsBomb), but marking sources disagree, many season-wide claims are retrospective (Breaking The Lines, These Football Times), and squad age/rotation and Heynckes's own tactical words are thin.
